claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child or children.

**How old is the child you want to claim Child Benefit for?**

- **Under 16 years old?**
- **16-19 years old?**
- **20 years old or over?**

Also, please let me know:
- The name(s) of the child/children you're inquiring about
- How many children are you claiming for?

This will help me guide you through the eligibility assessment accurately.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son, Alex. He's 8 years old, so under 16. It's just the one child I'm asking about.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're inquiring about **Alex**, who is **8 years old** (under 16). Let me navigate through the eligibility checks for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Since Alex is under 16, I need to check the following:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

(This is a standard eligibility check - children who work 24 or more hours per week may not qualify, but this is unlikely to apply to an 8-year-old!)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 8, so he's just at primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I'd expect for an 8-year-old. Let me continue with the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check another requirement:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?** 

Specifically, is he NOT receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (in his own name/right)

(For an 8-year-old, this would be unusual, but I need to confirm for the eligibility check.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't get any benefits in his own name - he's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I'd expect. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! The next check is about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex NOT in an apprenticeship?** 

(Given that he's only 8 years old and in primary school, I'd imagine he's not in an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8! He's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense. Let me move forward to the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important requirement about **residency**:

**Does the claimant (you, as the person claiming Child Benefit for Alex) meet UK residency requirements?**

Here are the main ways you could qualify:

1. **Normally live in the UK** - This is the most common situation
2. **Have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **Have pre-settled status AND are working** (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months)
4. **Have pre-settled status AND are actively seeking work** (can claim for up to 91 days)
5. **Have pre-settled status with sufficient resources** (and NOT claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit)
6. **Have pre-settled status AND studying** (with sufficient resources)
7. **Have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national** (with right to reside)
8. **Living abroad as a Crown servant** (in qualifying countries)

Which of these applies to your situation? Or in simple terms: **Do you normally live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the most straightforward residency situation. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm that you're responsible for Alex. 

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means one or more of the following:

1. **You live with Alex** - This is the most common situation for parents
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - Such as paying for food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, or other care costs at least to the level of Child Benefit payments
3. **You're paying maintenance** - Under a court order or agreement toward Alex's care that equals or exceeds Child Benefit payments

Which of these applies to you? For example, do you live with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That confirms you're responsible for Alex. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check whether there are any other claimants for Alex:

**Is there anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim for him?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent also claiming?
- Does someone else have custody or responsibility who might be claiming?

Or is it just you claiming for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's just me - nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check where Alex is living:

**Where is Alex currently living?**

- **In hospital?**
- **In care?** (such as residential care)
- **Fostered?** (with foster carers)
- **Living normally at home with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living normally at home with me - just a regular home situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's a straightforward situation. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost there. I just need to check one final requirement:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Is the council NOT paying for Alex's housing?
- Is the council NOT paying for his care or upkeep?

(For most families, the answer would be "no, the council isn't paying" - but I need to confirm this.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything for him - I'm just raising him myself at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful! That's the final check completed. Let me now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! 🎉

## **YOU ARE ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT FOR ALEX**

Based on the eligibility assessment, you meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for your 8-year-old son, Alex. Here's why:

✅ **Alex is under 16 years old** - Automatic qualification  
✅ **Alex is not working full-time** - At primary school  
✅ **Alex is not receiving benefits in his own name** - Standard for a child  
✅ **Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship** - Too young  
✅ **You normally live in the UK** - Based in Manchester  
✅ **You are responsible for Alex** - He lives at home with you  
✅ **No one else is claiming for Alex** - Just you  
✅ **Alex is living normally at home** - Regular home situation  
✅ **The council is not paying for his accommodation/maintenance** - You're providing for him

---

## **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** or by post using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate**
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through self-assessment tax
5. **Payment frequency** - Child Benefit is paid every 4 weeks (or weekly in certain circumstances)

For more information and to apply, visit: **https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim**

Congratulations on qualifying for Child Benefit for Alex! 👶
